subtopic: Sum of cubes when the sum is zero
text: Let $a, b, c$ be real numbers such that $$a + b + c = \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b} + \frac{1}{c}$$ and $abc = 5$. The value of $\left(a - \frac{1}{b}\right)^3 + \left(b - \frac{1}{c}\right)^3 + \left(c - \frac{1}{a}\right)^3$ can be written in the form $\frac{m}{n}$, where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers. Find $m + n$.
